model_annotation: This plot compares the performance of multiple methods—FT, IKE, MEMIT, ROME, and two additional unlabeled lines (black and brown)—across a logarithmically scaled x-axis. The x-axis appears to span from approximately 10⁰ to beyond 10³, with tick marks visible at 10¹, 10², and 10³, though the axis labels are partially obscured. The y-axis labels are also obscured, making the exact scale and units indeterminate, but the axis appears to use a linear scale. The ROME line (green, solid, with square markers) starts at a relatively high value on the left side of the plot, rises steeply to its highest visible point around 10¹, and then continues upward before being cut off at the right edge of the plot where it reaches the top of the chart area. The MEMIT line (purple, solid, with diamond markers) begins at a moderate value near the left, increases steadily across the x-axis, and reaches a value near the upper portion of the plot at 10³. The brown line (solid, with diamond markers) starts at a value similar to MEMIT on the left, increases gradually, and ends at approximately the same level as or slightly above MEMIT at the rightmost point. The IKE line (red, solid, with triangle markers) starts at a low-to-moderate value and increases gradually, ending at a moderate level at 10³. The FT line (blue, solid, with inverted triangle markers) begins at a low value and shows a gradual upward trend, ending slightly below IKE at the right side. The black line (solid, with circle markers) starts at the lowest value on the left and shows the most gradual increase, remaining the lowest line throughout the entire range of the x-axis. All lines exhibit generally increasing trends from left to right, with varying rates of increase.
